trigger: Ander Etcheverry walks out to talk.

nodes.speaker: ander
nodes.text: Ander Etcheverry. Lahontan Compact. I want to talk to the mechanic, not the Army.

nodes.speaker: ander
nodes.text: Thirty trucks of food leave Nevada tonight. Our old people eat sagebrush tea. Explain to me the justice.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Your father. Behind the bales. Older than three months should have made him. A rifle across his chest.

nodes.speaker: ross
nodes.text: You got my letter. ...You came anyway. On their side.

choices.text: I'm on nobody's side. I fix trucks.
I'm on Carly's side. Reno's side.
Get off the road, Dad. Please.

nodes.speaker: ross
nodes.text: That's the lie everybody tells right before they pick a side.

nodes.speaker: ross
nodes.text: Reno's side. Okay. Your mother would've liked her. That doesn't change the road.

nodes.speaker: ross
nodes.text: Can't. Every rancher in Mason Valley is behind me. I made them promises.

nodes.speaker: ander
nodes.text: Your father is a good man. He's the reason half these men came. Think about that.

nodes.speaker: ander
nodes.text: So. Do the trucks roll, or do they stay in Nevada?

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: The MRAPs push. The Compact fires. You fire back, because they're firing at you. Your father is out there.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: You pull the fuel line on the lead truck. It dies across both lanes. Ruiz looks at you for a long second.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Fifteen trucks peel off toward Sparks. The Army doesn't know who to shoot. Everyone shoots a little.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: When the shooting stops, the bales are burning. You don't see your father. You don't see Wes either.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Then you hear him. Wes. Screaming your name from under the overpass.
